---
description: Coarse junk-cut of discovered jobs before the expensive matcher, run by the hunt orchestrator
---
<!-- generated by `python -m src.hunt sync-agents` from prompts/commands/jh-triage.md; edit that file, not this one -->

Cheaply triage newly discovered jobs so the real matcher (`/jh-match`) only spends tokens on
plausibly-relevant roles. The hunt orchestrator does the work (`python -m src.hunt`,
`docs/spec-hunt-orchestrator.md`): it exports the untriaged pile into 100-row chunks, runs one
triager process per chunk on the harness and model in `config/hunt.toml` (the rubric is
`prompts/agents/triager.md`), checks that every out file covers every id of its chunk, retries
the short ones and ingests. Drops land at `status='irrelevant'` (gone from every future stage);
keepers carry a 0-3 fit bucket that later orders scoring. You are the viewer: do not start
agents, read chunks or write out files yourself. Use `.venv/bin/python` if plain `python` is not
on PATH.

1. **Start it**: run `python -m src.hunt run --only triage` with your shell tool, in the
   background if your shell tool can (a large pile runs for many minutes). If the last triage
   run stopped early, continue it with `python -m src.hunt run --resume latest` instead:
   finished chunks are skipped and nothing is exported twice. "another hunt holds the lock"
   means a run is already going; go to step 2.

2. **Watch it**: `python -m src.hunt status latest`, at most once every two minutes, and relay
   the units done of total and any unit on a retry and why. Do not tail logs or open the ledger.

3. **Report**: when the command exits, run `python -m src.hunt report latest` and relay the
   triage line: kept vs dropped, the bucket split, any failed chunk. The stage is skipped when
   the pile is under `min_pile` in `config/hunt.toml`; say so plainly when that happened. Exit 2
   means a chunk failed: offer `python -m src.hunt run --resume latest`.

Next: `/jh-match` scores the survivors, ordered by fit bucket (best first).
